compose._doc_post_hook: Provisioning assertion, deliberately SEPARATE from init.sh. init.sh is the maddy container's entrypoint and ends in `exec maddy`, so it cannot exit non-zero on a provisioning failure without turning a missing mailbox into a total mail outage; it only emits a SUMMARY receipt into the maddy_data volume. assert-provisioning.sh reads that receipt on the host, rejects one written before the current container start, and fails the SHIP if any *_failed > 0 or users_ok = 0 — while maddy keeps serving. Gated in turn by the engine's revision-scoped post-hook receipt, so a hook that never ran is not green either.

lifecycle._doc: Post-hoc maintenance via mail-sieve-subset-post-hoc.sh. SQL-direct on /data/imapsql.db using the actual go-imap-sql schema. UNIFIED-INBOX delivery model: maddy delivery-time always places mail in INBOX (with \Seen via inbox_copy_flags from mail-rules.json); apply-rules then SQL-direct COPIES (NOT moves) into matched category folders with rule-derived keywords (no \Seen — copies are unread). INBOX is the chronological archive; category folders are the unread working set. apply-rules is idempotent via the $distributed keyword on the INBOX original — maddy-sorter (src/crate, Rust, compiled into this same image via docker.native_build) runs the equivalent logic continuously (started by init.sh alongside `maddy run`, no external scheduler); the bash cmd_apply_rules / post-hoc-apply-rules lifecycle entries below are for manual/testing use only now. reseed-inbox-archive is a one-shot history backfill that COPIES every existing non-system folder msg back into INBOX as \Seen + $distributed (Message-Id deduped). recover-headers stays intentionally NOT a subcommand: missing-blob bodies are unrecoverable, integrity-fix is the right action.

l4_ports.comment: SMTP MX plain TCP — design-complete listener; GCP firewall currently blocks public, CF Worker is the active inbound bridge

primary._doc_l4_ports: Only :25 lives here — Maddy still answers plain SMTP. The imap./smtps. SNI routes on :443 moved to user-comm_tools-stalwart/build.json, which is what actually terminates them (imaps -> Stalwart :2993 since 2026-09-02, smtps -> Stalwart :2465). A route is declared by the service that answers the bytes.

app._doc_dual_bind: Phase 4 of public-surface collapse: each port dual-binds on wg0 (10.0.0.3) AND wg-public (10.1.0.3). Maddy is host-network so binds happen inside maddy.conf.tpl via `@LISTEN_<port>@`; flake.nix expands `bind` arrays into space-separated multi-listener prefixes (e.g. `tls://10.0.0.3:993 tls://10.1.0.3:993`). Caddy on oci-analytics reaches mail ports via wg-public; legacy clients on wg0 keep working unchanged.

extra_ports.desc: MX delivery endpoint — dual-bind wg0+wg-public; CF Worker → Caddy → http-to-smtp-proxy-api → SMTP over WG is the public bridge (Phase 5)
Direct inbound leg of the CF Worker parallel fan-out (#1811): stores in maddy only, no Stalwart mirror (Stalwart gets its own leg). WG-only.
SMTPS — dual-bind wg0+wg-public, reached via Caddy L4 from oci-analytics
IMAPS — dual-bind wg0+wg-public, reached via Caddy L4 from oci-analytics

resources._doc_mem_limit: Measured on oci-mail 2026-10-13: anon <=30MiB (6MiB resident + 24MiB swapped), cgroup peak 171MiB of which nearly all was reclaimable page cache over imapsql.db. 128M bounds the cache without touching the working set; it replaces the 2G category default, which on a 954MiB VM capped nothing. Gate: _shared/test-mail-stack-limits.mjs. 128M -> 192M (2026-11-18 oci-mail incident: load 13, IO PSI ~75%, maddy 145GB read / 29GB written lifetime). At 128M the cgroup could not hold the imapsql.db page cache next to maddy-sorter's full-file backups, so the DB was re-read from disk on every pass. 192M keeps the four mail ceilings at 704MiB, inside the 954MiB box with the 250MiB host reserve (L7). The backups are now rate-limited too (BACKUP_MIN_INTERVAL).
resources._doc_reservation: 32M -> 96M (2026-11-18 21:00, oci-mail IO PSI some 78; maddy's cgroup reading 832KB/s while the maddy process itself read 0KB/s, i.e. page-cache refaults of imapsql.db and its own binary after host-wide reclaim). Docker renders reservations.memory as cgroup v2 memory.low, so under host pressure the kernel reclaims unprotected cache elsewhere before maddy's first 96M. It is a reclaim floor, not an allocation, and the 192M ceiling is unchanged. SQLite settings were checked and are no lever here: maddy 0.9's storage.imapsql sqlite3_cache_size is parsed but never applied by the pinned go-imap-sql (8da5567, Opts.CacheSize has no reader), and nothing sets mmap_size, so imapsql.db is read through the page cache, which is exactly what memory.low protects. Mail-stack reservations total 256M of 954M (stalwart 128, maddy 96, sorter 16, puller 16). Gate: _shared/test-mail-stack-limits.mjs R3/R4.

docker._doc: Was Type-B (FROM foxcpp/maddy:0.9 + apk add, no compile). Now native_build: same base image (still gets maddy itself for free from upstream), same apk packages (moved from runtime_packages -- that field only fed the Type-B auto-detect path, which native_build.type bypasses entirely), PLUS an in-container compile of maddy-sorter (src/crate) copied in alongside. One image, both binaries -- maddy-sorter's own code lives in this service's src/, same as jmap-sorter does for Stalwart.

native_build._doc_builder_image: MUST be an alpine/musl builder, not rust:1-bookworm (glibc) -- base_image below is foxcpp/maddy:0.9 (alpine/musl). A glibc-linked binary copied into a musl final image has no dynamic linker to run against (this isn't a PATH issue patchelf can fix, unlike the nix-store-ld-linux case elsewhere in this repo -- glibc and musl are different libcs, not just different paths to the same one). rust:1-alpine's native target already IS x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, so no --target flag or cross toolchain needed, just a C compiler for libsqlite3-sys's build script (rusqlite's "bundled" feature compiles its own sqlite3.c) -- hence build-base in cmd below.
native_build._doc_apk: jq/sqlite/coreutils are for the OTHER post-hoc subcommands (integrity-check, dedupe, cleanup-mailboxes, reseed-inbox-archive), which stay bash + sqlite3-CLI. maddy-sorter itself needs neither -- rusqlite's bundled feature compiles its own libsqlite3, no apk sqlite required for apply-rules specifically.

stalwart_relay._doc: #1821: where maddy's durable stalwart_queue delivers its Stalwart copy (target.smtp stalwart_relay, plain SMTP :2025 over the mesh). Stalwart moved from oci-mail (10.0.0.3) to oci-apps; the address is the oci-apps wg0 IP and the port is Stalwart's smtp_shadow listener. Pinned to user-comm_tools-stalwart/build.json by _shared/test-stalwart-host.mjs (C2).

deliver-parity.cmd: cargo build --release --manifest-path src/crate/Cargo.toml && python3 src/test-deliver-parity.py src/crate/target/release/maddy-sorter
deliver-parity._doc: #1883: the Rust `maddy-sorter deliver` must answer exactly like the shell classifier mail-sieve-subset-delivery-time.sh (jq + awk) on every generated rules x message x MAIL_SIEVE_STRATEGY combination: same stdout bytes, same exit status. The shell script is the unmodified reference; the harness exits 2 when a tool is missing or the corpus is too weak, it never skips.

integrity-parity.cmd: cargo build --release --manifest-path src/crate/Cargo.toml && bash src/test-integrity-parity.sh src/crate/target/release/maddy-sorter
integrity-parity._doc: #1883: `maddy-sorter integrity-check` (read-only, rusqlite) must print the same report as the shell `mail-sieve-subset-post-hoc integrity-check` (sqlite3 CLI + sort/comm/awk) on clean, broken and empty databases, and must not modify the database.
